key: When Indra and the Angirases desired it, Sarama found provision for her offspring.
s: Praising Indra, through whom the Angirases found the cattle, the hymn tells of the search; Sāyaṇa, on 1.62.3, reads it through the tale of Sarama, the gods’ hound, sent after the cows the Paṇis stole, going only once Indra promised their milk to her young.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.62.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400586 (2024)

evidence.words: अत्रेदमाख्यानम् । सरमा नाम देवशुनी । पणिभिर्गोष्वपहृतासु तद्गवेषणाय तां सरमामिन्द्रः प्रहैषीत्। यथा लोके व्याधो वनान्तर्गतमृगान्वेषणाय श्वानं विसृजति तद्वत् । सा च सरमा एवमवोचत्। हे इन्द्र अस्मदीयाय शिशवे तद्गोसंबन्धि क्षीराद्यन्नं यदि प्रयच्छसि तर्हि गमिष्यामीति । स तथेत्यब्रवीत्
evidence.gloss: Here is the story. Saramā is the name of the gods’ bitch. When the cows had been carried off by the Paṇis, Indra sent Saramā to search for them, as in the world a hunter lets loose a dog to track the deer in the forest. And Saramā said: Indra, if you give my young one food from those cows, milk and the like, then I will go. He said: so be it.
